decisions.reason: As a 2023-launched handle family in the firm’s core range, it should be kept because market uncertainty is still high while the cost of maintaining an incremental design variant is likely low.
The mitred handle family fits the company’s architecture-led portfolio, and after only one year there is too little evidence to justify abandonment of a relatively low-cost option.
Its multifunctional positioning aligns with the firm’s system-solution strategy, so management would keep the product while learning more about demand before making a final commitment.
With no negative market signal reported and only a short time since launch, keeping this core door lever preserves upside at limited additional cost.
This collection has the strongest early validation through its dedicated presentation and German Design Award win, which supports further commercialization rather than exit.
A new finish is inexpensive to carry relative to a wholly new product and expands the firm’s coordinated design offering, so it remains a worthwhile option to keep open.
